newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa gets jobs fillip from Telkom deal.
newsitem.headline: South Africa gets jobs fillip from Telkom deal.

text.p: The partial privatisation of state utility Telkom, finalised on Wednesday, will provide a badly-needed employment boost to the South African economy.

Telkom and its strategic equity partners SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd, who are to take a 30 percent stake, say some 50,000 jobs will be created in the telcommunications sector alone.

"We've given an enormous boost to the economy. This deal will stimulate investor confidence in the country and provide a major boost to jobs," Posts, Telecommunications and Broadcasting Minister Jay Naidoo told Reuters.

Despite four years of successive growth, the South African economy is continuing to shed jobs. Formal employment has increased only once during any calendar year since 1989 when it rose by 0.7 percent in 1995.

Total employment in the formal non-agricultural sectors of the economy declined by 1.4 percent in the the third quarter of 1996, after declines of 1.1 percent in the second quarter and 3.9 percent in the first, according to the Reserve Bank.
Unemployment is estimated at around 30 percent of a workforce of some 15 million. New jobs are outpaced by a third of a million school leavers a year.
The government's macroeconomic strategy, unveiled last June, aims to create 400,000 jobs a year by the turn of the century by doubling economic growth to six percent.
